item.title: Julieta Venegas, Trueno, Milo J & More: Your Guide to LAMC 2026 in New York City
item.description:
[Energetic music fades out, and the host's voice takes over]
Host: "Welcome to our podcast, where we dive into the world of music and culture. Today, we're talking about the Latin Alternative Music Conference, or LAMC, and its home in the vibrant city of New York. For decades, NYC has been a hub for Latin music, with genres like salsa, reggaetón, and Latin rock thriving in the city that never sleeps."
[Short music transition]
Host: "The LAMC was founded in 2000 by Tomas Cookman and Josh Norek, and it's grown into a unique industry gathering where emerging artists, executives, managers, and fans come together. As Cookman says, 'It's where indies, majors, and a kaleidoscope of genres and artists meet.' The conference has evolved over the years, from its focus on alternative music to embracing the mainstream Latin music scene."
[Short music transition]
Host: "So, what can you expect from LAMC 2026? The conference offers a range of activities, from daytime panels and evening showcases to off-site events and free public concerts. You can catch live performances by artists like Julieta Venegas, Trueno, and La India, and network with industry professionals. Whether you're looking to discover new music or connect with others in the industry, LAMC has something for everyone."
[Closing music starts playing]
Host: "So, mark your calendars for LAMC 2026 and get ready to experience the best of Latin alternative music in the city that never sleeps. We'll be back with more updates and behind-the-scenes stories from the conference. Thanks for tuning in, and we'll catch you on the next episode!"
[Music fades out]
